chosen.text: Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.

candidates.text: Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.
candidates.context: Paul to the churches of Galatia; a call to mutual, embodied care within the church, right after instruction on restoring someone caught in sin gently.
candidates.whyItFits: Speaks directly to the heart of a handoff: burdens are carried by people in community, not by a tool. Fits the theme of bearing one another's burdens.

candidates.text: Where there is no wise guidance, the nation falls, but in the multitude of counselors there is victory.
candidates.context: Solomonic proverb to Israel's covenant community about wisdom in leadership and decisions.
candidates.whyItFits: Affirms the value of many wise counselors; supports guardrails and handoffs to pastors, though its original setting is national leadership.

candidates.text: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him who is alone when he falls, and doesn’t have another to lift him up.
candidates.context: The Teacher reflecting on toil and isolation, addressed to general readers.
candidates.whyItFits: Fits a person in crisis needing someone to lift them up, but is more general than the ministry/counsel theme.
